sites.rationale: L1 names G199/S201 as one of the tolerated pHluorin insertion sites in EL2. Canonical sequence shows seq[199]=G and seq[200]=D (not S); seq[201]=S. The junction is placed after G199 (insert_after_residue=199), with residue_after=D. The paper's 'S201' likely refers to the second flanking residue or reflects a minor numbering offset; the G199 anchor is unambiguous. Position is within EL2 (165–235), 35 residues from TM3 end. Full-length human DAT with pHluorin inserted at G199/S201 in EL2 (one of five sites screened); the paper labels this junction 'G199/S201' but canonical sequence has seq[199]=G, seq[200]=D, seq[201]=S, so the junction is after G199.

sources.claim: Flexible linkers were inserted on both ends of pHluorin to introduce additional flexibility for the proper folding of the reporter. pHluorin was inserted at multiple sites, T173/E174, P194/G195, G199/S201, G209/T210, R219/G220 outside the known functional sites of DAT. 45 , 46 , 47 , 48 Although some insertion sites (T173/E174, G209/T210) resulted in poor expression of the transgene in the initial screen, little difference was observed for the remaining versions of DAT-pHluorin (DAT-pH) in their overall expression patterns (data not shown).

sites.rationale: L10 confirms that the HA tag in full-length YFP-HA-DAT is extracellularly accessible at the plasma membrane by non-permeabilized antibody staining. L9 shows AIM-100-induced redistribution from plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles, confirming functional trafficking. The HA is in EL2 (per L7 which replaces it with HA-βlac in the same loop), but no residue junction is named, so the site is reported at the loop level. Full-length YFP-HA-DAT stably expressed in PAE cells; HA tag in EL2 detected at plasma membrane surface by anti-HA antibody staining of non-permeabilized cells (Cy5 channel). No specific residue junction stated for the HA position.

sources.claim: After fixation, cultures were stained with secondary anti-mouse antibodies conjugated with Cy5 ( surface HA-DAT ), permeabilized with Triton X-100 and stained with secondary anti-mouse conjugated with Cy3 ( internalized HA-DAT ). 3D images were acquired through 488 (YFP, not shown), 561 (Cy3, red ) and 640 nm (Cy5, cyan ) channels.

literature_notes: Seven sites are reported. The primary validated site is P194/G195 in EL2 (L2+L3: pHluorin, surface+function confirmed). Two additional exact-residue sites in EL3 (P288) and EL4 (P387) are grounded in tetraCys labeling (L4/L5). Two further EL2 sites (G199, R219) are grounded in the same pHluorin screen (L1) but with weaker validation (expression only). Two region-level EL2 sites are reported for BBS (L6) and HA/HA-βlac (L10) insertions from independent papers. L11 (Twin-Strep-HA downstream of AttR2 in vector) was not used: the tag position within the DAT protein cannot be pinned from the clip. L12 (C-terminal FLAG) is reported in other_positions as intracellular. The N-terminal YFP in YFP-HA-DAT (L9) is intracellular (residues 1–68 are cytoplasmic) and is also in other_positions. The paper's notation 'G199/S201' was resolved by sequence lookup: seq[199]=G, seq[200]=D, seq[201]=S; the junction is placed after G199.

literature_other_positions.note: pHluorin insertion at T173/E174 resulted in poor expression of the transgene in the initial screen, indicating this junction disrupts folding or trafficking.

C-terminal FLAG tag on DAT detected by ELISA; the DAT C-terminus (residues 579–620) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
YFP fused to the N-terminus of DAT in YFP-HA-DAT; the DAT N-terminus (residues 1–68) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so the N-terminal YFP faces the cytoplasm.
